pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as 30-40 minutes, three to four times a week, strength/conditioning/mobility in one unit, with short daily mobility protocols and a six-month term justified by technique acquisition and habit formation. The prospect accepted the logic ('Yeah, I think that makes sense') and then asked a genuine mechanics question about what happens afterwards: 'Does he continuously work with other people? Can or could you stay on past six months if you were interested in staying on?' The rep confirmed continuation is possible but gave no price or structure for it. Notably the rep also volunteered a safety caveat here — 'Kettlebells are not some magical solution. You can get injured with them also' — without connecting it to the bilateral ACL history disclosed eighteen minutes earlier.

Volunteered a positive reaction and tied it to his own existing practice: 'No, I like that. I appreciate it. I mean, those are fundamental things that I agree with. So, yeah... I'm glad to hear similar philosophies around nutrition.' He had already told the rep he fasts until noon and prefers one or two large meals, so the intermittent-fasting framing landed as confirmation rather than instruction. The rep also correctly picked the one live risk in his diet — protein intake — and flagged that real food is preferable to shakes, which the prospect agreed with.

The pillar he came for, and the rep said so explicitly — 'the last bit, the one that you came here for, which is accountability.' Response: 'Yeah, that sounds great. Yeah, it sounds like what I want. And... philosophically, I agree with all those points.' This was pre-sold: twenty minutes earlier he had already articulated the mechanism himself — 'having an external person to hold you accountable to, that you're paying, that you're committed to, that you respect... will get you the extra 20% of effort that I currently am not using.' The rep's 'he's going to be knocking on your phone and asking you, hey, Eddy, where you been?' matched the prospect's own stated model of how he performs best.

anchors.raw: I think the coaching I've had in the past, which is, I agree, probably not at that standard, was like $500 a month, and I think that's the price I have in my head
anchors.competitor: a previous personal coach (bodybuilding and nutrition focus), used roughly six years ago
anchors.note: The operative anchor of the entire call and it was never addressed. He states it at the moment of price reveal and restates it eleven minutes later — 'probably because all the coaching I've had is usually like 500 a month' — which means he spent the whole objection sequence privately comparing $1,000/month against $500/month with no counter-argument ever supplied. He even pre-conceded the quality difference ('probably not at that standard'), which was an open invitation to build the premium case. Nobody took it.

anchors.raw: I've reached out to a couple of coaches, including you guys ... there was one bodybuilder guy and another guy that didn't hit me back who was more CrossFit. So I'm just waiting on his response. But I like to at least talk to a few different people.
anchors.competitor: an ex-coach (bodybuilding/nutrition) and an unnamed CrossFit coach
anchors.note: A live, disclosed competitive evaluation. The rep asked one good qualifying question and established that neither competitor does kettlebells and that the prospect prefers Trevor's content most — then never used any of it. This is a differentiation opportunity that was surfaced and abandoned.

anchors.raw: I just bought a tractor for $10,000. I just bought something else for $10,000. I got to buy all this for that amount of money.
anchors.note: Two recent purchases at 1.6x the programme price, volunteered while explaining the objection. The rep used it correctly and immediately — 'So the money is there. That's for sure' — and it was not disputed. This is the evidence that the blocker is psychological rather than financial, and it is what justified the regret frame that followed.

anchors.raw: and it's $6,000 up front. Is that accurate? Or is it $1,000 a month?
anchors.note: Fourth prospect in this batch to convert $6,000 into a monthly figure within seconds of hearing it, and the third to land on $1,000/month specifically. Buyers are consistently not processing this as a six-month lump sum. The rep's answer defaulted to 'most of the guys put it up front', which surrenders the monthly frame rather than either owning it or reframing it.

anchors.raw: Especially that you have dumbbells and everything, like, you can do it on your own. Come on, man.
anchors.note: Rep-introduced while role-playing the wife's likely objection, and the prospect confirmed it as accurate ('Yeah, which is a fair point'). He has a fully equipped home gym, trains almost daily and has not needed a gym since COVID. The offer's entire premium therefore rests on programming and supervision, not access — which the prospect understands and agrees with ('but I've been trying to do it on my own my whole life, and I think I need help').

anchors.raw: So I'm starting a company and I'm just starting to take a salary and that's a huge part of it.
anchors.note: The real constraint, disclosed forty minutes in and only under pressure. It is a timing problem with an obvious commercial answer — a deposit plus instalments across the six months — which the rep had already offered twice in principle and never once structured.

anchors.raw: I like Trevor's content. I like the way he works out. I like work out really similarly. ... I think I like Trevor's content and what he's preaching the most, I guess.
anchors.note: Trevor's content is why he is on the call and why he ranks this option above two competitors. The rep reinforced it with his own conviction and personal story rather than with proof points, which the prospect received warmly — 'You're a tough cookie, man' — though he had earlier misremembered the coach's name as 'Tyler', suggesting the attachment is to the content rather than the person.

unmet_demand.want: Certainty of outcome before committing $6,000, which he named as his single highest priority over speed or cost
unmet_demand.why_unmet: A guarantee was produced, but improvised mid-objection and stated in two materially different scopes within about thirty seconds — first as adding at least 8 kg to baseline kettlebell movements, then as losing the 15-20 lb weight goal. It is not clear from the call which version is real, whether either is contractual, or what the compliance conditions are beyond 'proper nutrition and showing up'. The prospect welcomed it and it did not close him, which suggests he did not fully credit it either.

unmet_demand.want: A structured payment that fits a founder just beginning to take a salary
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Splitting was offered twice in principle and never built. No deposit amount, instalment count, schedule or total was ever discussed, so the prospect had nothing concrete to take to his wife. He explicitly said he was looking for exactly this — 'let me see if I can put together something that I can get to' — and was left to construct it himself.

unmet_demand.want: Programming for specific endurance events — a major canoe race about a year out, plus rucking and skiing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised early and in detail as his next big athletic target and never referenced again. The offer as presented is a general kettlebell strength, conditioning and mobility programme with a fat-loss orientation; whether it periodises toward a named endurance event, or would conflict with that training, was never established.

unmet_demand.want: Training that protects two previously torn ACLs and avoids joint replacement in his fifties
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Disclosed clearly, including his stated reason for abandoning running, and never addressed. No question about surgical history, current knee function, or whether loaded ballistic and jumping movements are appropriate. The programme may well suit him better than running does, but nobody said so, and nobody checked.

unmet_demand.want: The option to continue with coaching beyond the six-month term
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly. The rep confirmed it happens ('There are some guys that want to stay for a year') but gave no price, no structure and no mechanism, and steered back to starting with six months. For a buyer whose stated model is that he performs best under permanent supervision, the six-months-then-you-are-on-your-own framing is arguably selling against his actual demand.
